title: Incorporation of Ru in BaTiO3 for Improved Electrocatalytic Activity
content: Energy consumption has surged in recent years due to industrialization and rapid population growth, along with social and technological advancements [1-3]. Electrocatalysis has been a renowned field for energy conversion and storage that plays vital role in various sustainable energy technologies and environmental applications like water splitting [1,2,4], fuel cells [5], batteries [6], CO2 reduction [3], supercapacitors [7] etc. for past few decades. Several researchers have explored different materials for applications in the field of electrocatalysis for the generation of alternative and sustainable sources of energy [8-10]. Among various investigated perovskite class of materials, BaTiO3 is considered as potential candidate for electrocatalysis because of its enhanced charge storage ability, locally enhanced electric field, piezoelectric characteristics, presence of oxygen vacancies in crystal structure, high charge transfer, high reactant adsorption on its surface, and high specific surface area [4,11,12]. One of the various methods used to improve electrocatalytic performance of BaTiO3 is doping it with various chemical elements, which opens up new possibilities for engineering the material's crystal properties for a range of applications [13,14]. BTiO3 is very prone to the substitution or doping of different metal ions at both sites because of the size differences between Ba and Ti, proving a crucial tool for controlling its carrier concentration [14]. Numerous studies also shown that BaTiO3 nanoparticles are extremely biocompatible and have very low toxicity [15].
